messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency SLO breach detected for /v1/generate in prod (us-west). Current p95=620ms (SLO 250ms), p99=1.9s (SLO 800ms). Alert triggered at 2026-03-15T14:12:58Z. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/prod/latency?range=5m :rotating_light:

maya (oncall): acked. I'm on it. Paging kevin and mike for infra/runtime checks.

kevin (sre): I'm up. grabbing traces. first glance: increased tail on streaming responses; a bunch of stalled connections showing long wait on kv-cache fetches.

mike (infra): Repro locally? any recent deploys to model-serving?

maya (oncall): no prod deploys in last 30m according to deploy-bot.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: No successful releases to prod in the last 60 minutes.

kevin (sre): running quick query on traces:
```
trace.query("service:inference AND route:/v1/generate AND latency>500")
```
results: spike concentrated on GPU pool pool-a and hosts ash-gpu-12..15.

kevin (sre): p95 jump looks correlated with increased queue time inside runtime (queue_ms). sample: queue_ms median 300 -> 850. kernel scheduling time also spiking.

maya (oncall): is this affecting streaming only or non-streaming too?

kevin (sre): mostly streaming. Non-streaming p95 uptick but p99 dominated by streaming stalls where client sees no tokens for >10s.

liz (support): getting customer reports: 3 active tickets flagged by enterprise customers Axiom & Drift — they see partial outputs or stalled streams.

sam (product): customer impact: high for chat use-cases. We should notify CS and account execs if this persists >30m.

maya (oncall): quick mitigation plan: 1) shift traffic off pool-a to pool-b (warm). 2) increase runtime replicas for streaming routes. 3) enable fallback routing to nolog-quantized model variant for streaming. I'll start 1 and 2.

mike (infra): starting drain of ash-gpu-12..15 from LB and spinning up 4 warm nodes in pool-b. ETA ~3m.

kevin (sre): while that's happening, toggling conservative batching (turn off multi-request batching) for streaming routes to reduce queue pressure. Command:
```
redwoodctl route update --route /v1/generate --config batching.enabled=false
```
Executing now.

maya (oncall): running health checks: curl -s -D - https://prod-api/redwood/health | head -n 20
Output: all services healthy but runtime queue depth high.

kevin (sre): logs from ash-gpu-13 (tail):
```
[14:11:45] runtime: kv-cache miss, fetching shard 7
[14:11:46] runtime: kernel-schedule wait 420ms
[14:12:02] stream: stall detected, client_id=xx-yyy
[14:12:15] runtime: error=deadline_exceeded processing request
```
pattern: burst of KV-cache contention and occasional deadline_exceeded on streaming.

mike (infra): warm nodes are up; shifting 30% traffic to pool-b now via traffic-router.

incident-bot: change applied: traffic-router rule active — /v1/generate: 30% -> pool-b.

maya (oncall): monitoring p95/p99 in dashboard.

kevin (sre): after throttling batching and shifting traffic, p95 dropped to ~320ms, p99 down to ~950ms. Still above SLO but trending.

liz (support): CS updated customers Axiom & Drift with mitigation steps and ETA. They asked for ETA on full resolution.

sam (product): messaging suggestion: "We’re experiencing degraded streaming performance; mitigation in progress. We'll update in 30 minutes or on resolution."

maya (oncall): next step: if p99 still > SLO after 10m, force fallback routing for streaming to quantized variant to keep latency predictable. Will we get a quality hit?

kevin (sre): small quality drop expected for open models quantized variant but likely acceptable short-term. Command to enable fallback:
```
redwoodctl routing set-fallback --route /v1/generate --variant gptx-quant-8bit
```
I will hold until after 10m of observation unless you want me to flip earlier.

maya (oncall): hold for 8m. I'm opening an incident ticket: https://inc.redwood/INC-2026-317 (assigned to oncall).

mike (infra): note: ash-gpu-14 showed high NVLink error counts — I’ll open a hardware ticket if errors persist after drain.

kevin (sre): 5m update: p95=280ms, p99=720ms, stream stall count dropped 78%. Looks stable.

liz (support): customers acknowledged — Axiom says partial improvements but asks for postmortem.

maya (oncall): OK keeping watch. I’m handing this to kevin for long-running follow-up and postmortem; I'll be available for handoff.

kevin (sre): taking over. I'll keep monitoring for 2 hours and start RCA. Immediate action items: 1) collect full KV-cache hit/miss histograms for pool-a. 2) correlate kernel selection changes. 3) confirm hardware error counts on drained nodes.

maya (oncall): handover noted. oncall -> kevin.

incident-bot: pager closed by maya (oncall) at 2026-03-15T14:25:35Z.

kevin (sre): creating incident doc and timeline. Tagging infra and runtime teams. Follow-ups: postmortem, hardware ticket if NVLink persists, and consider more conservative batching defaults for streaming routes.

sam (product): please include customer-visible timeline for CS.

kevin (sre): will do. I'll post an initial incident summary in ~45m and assign owners for RCA actions.

liz (support): thx — I'll queue the customer notes.

mike (infra): hardware ticket opened for ash-gpu-12..15 (HW-4321).

kevin (sre): final quick note: if anyone sees a re-spike, immediately flip fallback routing to quantized variant and re-scale until we confirm kernel/kv fixes.

mike (infra): noted.

incident-bot: NOTE: this thread will be used as the live coordination channel for the incident. Please avoid creating duplicate threads."
